name: SourceLens
description: A domain-specific, extractive RAG application that turns uploaded PDFs into evidence-constrained answers with physical page citations. It addresses a practical problem: language models can sound certain even when the source does not support an answer.
features: Page-aware PDF extraction and bounded uploads
Quotation validation, citations and insufficient-evidence refusal
Session-isolated collections and explicit cloud-provider consent
decisions: Normalized embeddings make inner-product search cosine-equivalent. FAISS keeps retrieval inspectable.
Qwen selects relevant excerpts; application code validates quotations and assembles the answer. This conservative design trades broad synthesis for traceable provenance.
Indexes and uploads stay in session memory; changing a collection disables chat until the new collection is processed.
challenges: Preserve physical page numbers when some pages have no readable text.
Separate invalid model output from an authentic insufficient-evidence refusal.
Rank compound question clauses separately to reduce topic crowding.
evaluation: Repository record: 34 automated tests and 12 browser checks.
Recorded development evaluation: 23/23 authored synthetic questions, including five refusal cases. 21 successful cases were retained and two rerun after a quotation-validation fix.
These are historical repository results, not an independent benchmark or tests rerun by this portfolio.
limitations: Citation provenance does not prove relevance or source truth.
Portfolio walkthrough uses recorded synthetic cases; it runs neither MiniLM nor Qwen.

name: CareerLens
description: An educational resume-analysis application that makes lexical skill matching transparent: identify documented skills, compare curated role profiles and turn missing terminology into a learning roadmap.
features: Hybrid coverage and TF-IDF cosine ranking
PDF/DOCX parsing and in-memory PDF reporting
decisions: Fit binary TF-IDF once on fixed role profiles, then project the resume onto each target’s skills. Unrelated skills cannot dilute the score.
Use 75% core coverage, 15% preferred coverage and 10% cosine similarity; use 90/10 when preferred requirements are absent.
Show contextual mentions without weighting prestige, protected attributes or inferred ability.
challenges: Preserve C++, C#, .NET and CI/CD punctuation during extraction.
Reject unsafe or oversized documents without persisting personal uploads.
Explain that a missing keyword is not proof of missing ability.
evaluation: Recorded evaluation: three fictional profiles exported in two formats; all six top-role checks matched.
The repository includes parser, scoring, monotonicity, PDF and UI tests and a recorded browser walkthrough.
Perfect fixture scores apply only to this small authored dataset.
limitations: Lexical matching does not establish proficiency, employability or hiring probability.
Portfolio executes the role-scoring formula on explicit skill selections; it does not parse resumes or reproduce the full Python application.
English technical roles; curated profiles are not live job vacancies.

name: FORM
description: A fitness workspace combining browser-side pose geometry, nutrition, habits and progress tracking with a TypeScript backend. Privacy is a concrete boundary: camera frames are processed locally rather than uploaded.
features: Six exercise geometries with complete-cycle rep detection
Local MediaPipe inference with visible landmarks
Habit indexes, schedules and progress reports
Tenant-scoped accounts, RBAC and session recovery
Optional FastAPI interoperability and simulated equipment
decisions: The authoritative backend uses TypeScript Workers and relational D1; FastAPI is an optional integration service.
Hold angle thresholds for 120 ms and require complete movement cycles before counting a rep.
Keep synthetic replay labelled and excluded from real activity and adherence analytics.
challenges: Degrade safely when camera or WebGL support is missing.
Maintain tenant and role boundaries across account, workout and administrative routes.
Treat geometric cues as unvalidated coaching heuristics rather than medical or safety guarantees.
evaluation: Repository record dated 28 September 2026: 80 automated tests plus 11 running-build HTTP checks passed.
Records cover geometry, nutrition, actual API handlers on SQLite, UI and Python interoperability.
Live webcam inference, physical equipment and external LLM calls were not verified.
limitations: Portfolio runs the original geometric replay engine on synthetic landmarks, with no camera or inference model.
Geometric thresholds have not been validated across users and camera placements.
Nutrition and movement outputs are educational estimates.

name: StudyBuddy AI
description: A deliberately small conversational study assistant connecting a Streamlit interface to Ollama and the local Llama 3.2 1B model. It explores the shortest useful path between a question and locally generated explanation.
features: Windows setup launcher and documented test prompts
decisions: Keep inference local instead of requiring an API key.
Keep the application intentionally simple: no database, authentication or retrieval pipeline.
challenges: Require a running Ollama service and an available local model.
Small language models can produce incorrect explanations.
evaluation: Four actual application screenshots and five documented test prompts are present.
No independent answer-quality benchmark is claimed.
limitations: Requires local model resources; no hosted model runs in this portfolio.
No RAG, durable conversations or authentication.

name: PyMentor AI
description: A console Python doubt solver demonstrating composable LangChain orchestration: validated question, controlled prompt, Gemini connector and string output parser.
features: Input limits and setup/API error handling
Offline self-test with explicit test doubles
decisions: Use the pipe operator to make the model pipeline readable.
Load provider credentials from environment configuration; never ship keys to a browser.
challenges: Handle unavailable provider models, quotas and empty outputs explicitly.
Separate offline pipeline checks from real API inference.
evaluation: Repository contains a self-test and five documented Python questions.
Offline test doubles validate flow; they do not establish live Gemini availability.
limitations: The portfolio shows a guided pipeline without sending requests to Gemini.
Original application needs a user-owned API key and network access; that dependency is not part of this zero-cost website.

name: Airbnb Price Regression
description: An educational linear-regression notebook on the New York City Airbnb 2019 dataset, covering preparation, feature engineering, held-out predictions and error analysis.
features: R², MAE, MSE and RMSE evaluation
decisions: Use a familiar baseline that exposes how features relate to nightly price.
Report absolute error as well as R² so readers can interpret prediction quality.
challenges: Skewed prices and incomplete listing attributes constrain the baseline.
A historical observational dataset cannot establish causal pricing effects.
evaluation: Stored executed notebook output: R² 0.4708; MAE $38.54; RMSE $53.24.
These describe the notebook’s prepared dataset and split, not future-market accuracy.
limitations: No deployed pricing service or exported browser model.
Portfolio metric explorer explains stored outputs; it does not generate listing valuations.

name: Diabetes · Logistic Regression
description: An educational classification experiment using the Pima diabetes dataset to study imputation, scaling, class balancing and evaluation tradeoffs. It is not a clinical diagnostic application.
decisions: Fit preprocessing inside a pipeline to avoid leakage from the held-out split.
Use class balancing and report recall alongside accuracy.
challenges: Distinguish model discrimination from clinical usefulness.
evaluation: Stored notebook output: accuracy 0.734, precision 0.603, recall 0.704, F1 0.650, ROC-AUC 0.813.
Test split contains 154 rows; metrics are rounded as recorded.
limitations: Educational dataset experiment only; no diagnosis or health recommendations.
No patient inputs are collected by the portfolio.

name: Diabetes · Random Forest
description: A tree-ensemble classification study with reproducible preprocessing, stratified tuning, feature importance and a held-out evaluation on the Pima dataset.
features: Stored confusion matrix and ROC curve
decisions: Tune using ROC-AUC inside cross-validation, then inspect an untouched held-out split.
Use n_jobs=1 in the notebook to bound resource use.
Report false negatives explicitly rather than relying on aggregate accuracy.
challenges: Account for invalid physiological zeros without leaking test statistics.
Feature importance is model-specific and does not imply causation.
evaluation: Recorded test outputs: 75.32% accuracy, 69.05% precision, 53.70% recall, 60.42% F1 and 0.8104 ROC-AUC.
Confusion matrix: TN 87, FP 13, FN 25, TP 29. Best five-fold CV ROC-AUC 0.8304.
limitations: Not a clinically validated diagnostic system.
Results are dataset- and split-specific; original training is not running in the browser.
